entry.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro from Moonshot AI is now available on Amazon Bedrock. Learn how to get started through the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, Responses, and Converse APIs, optimize inference with explicit prompt caching, and use the model as a coding assistant in OpenCode.

entry.title: Build a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search
entry.summary: The Web Search API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gives agents current, cited web results signed with the AWS credentials they already use. In this post, build a daily dependency watcher as a LangGraph graph that researches package ecosystems in parallel, keeps its rules in code, and checks every finding against its cited sources.

entry.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
entry.summary: When you deploy an agent, whether it is working is really several questions: did it finish the task, stay on topic, leak data, or skip steps? This post shows how to evaluate agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval evaluators, and how to match each behavior that matters to the right evaluator at the right level.

entry.title: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
entry.summary: Learn how Trovata built autonomous treasury agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using an RBAC-secured architecture for bank-branded AI deployment and agentic workflows that move corporate treasury from manual operations to real-time decision-making at enterprise scale.

entry.title: How TCS built an agentic test orchestrator with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) built an agentic test orchestrator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that turns requirements into executable, governed tests for its Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) clients. Learn how specialized agents, per-tenant isolation, and workload-aware execution cut testing effort by 88% in an internal benchmark.

entry.title: Amazon Bedrock tokenomics data lake
entry.summary: Running Amazon Bedrock across many accounts shows you the bill but not what happened inside each call. This post builds a centralized observability data lake that aggregates Bedrock invocation logs from every linked account into one queryable table, so you can see prompts, token counts, model choice, and per-invocation cost across your organization.

entry.title: How skills and agents work in AWS Quick
entry.summary: Repeatable tasks like status updates, release notes, and ticket creation can be encoded in AWS Quick through agents and skills. This post covers how agents, skills, and your data fit together in AWS Quick, how to build and share skills for your team, and how the official catalog and custom agents help you use them.

entry.title: Single-shot and agentic retrieval with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports single-shot RAG and retrieval-only requests through AgenticRetrieveStream, alongside agentic retrieval. This post explains how the maxAgentIteration parameter matches retrieval effort to each request, using an illustrative internal banking policy assistant.

entry.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
entry.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Learn what's new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with it on Amazon Bedrock.

entry.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
entry.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B-parameter multimodal vision-language model, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. Deploy the NVFP4 or BF16 variant in a few steps, then run text, image, and video inference for document intelligence, computer-use agents, and multimodal agentic workloads.

entry.title: Pluggable Agentic AI Framework: A seven-layer composable enterprise agentic AI reference architecture on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: A seven-layer composable reference architecture for taking enterprise agentic AI from prototype to production on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each layer has a stable contract, so you can swap technologies at any layer without redesigning the rest of the stack.

entry.title: How CrossnoKaye grounds physical AI with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: CrossnoKaye brought physical AI to heavy industry with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Its ATLAS platform and AURA agentic system ground AI reasoning in live plant data and run verifiable Python in isolated AgentCore sandboxes, giving plant engineers checkable, math-backed answers instead of model guesses.

entry.title: Professional work deserves professional tools. Meet AWS Quick.
entry.summary: Introducing AWS Quick, formerly Amazon Quick, and the debut of our first brand campaign celebrating teams who keep business moving. AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work, where teams use AI agents to research, analyze, and act across the data and applications they already rely on.

entry.title: SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker Inference now supports GPU partitioning with NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which divides one GPU into hardware-isolated partitions so you can run a different model in each or take a right-sized fraction of a newer accelerator. This post shows how two optional API fields place one model per partition, and what we measured against a whole older GPU.

entry.title: Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick
entry.summary: As we built Amazon Quick, its agents grew from answering questions to taking actions, and the same primitives kept getting rebuilt under different names. This post shares the taxonomy we converged on — triggers, agents, capabilities, and learned context — found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When, What, Who, and How.

entry.title: Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate
entry.summary: Learn how to build a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate that gives AI agents secure, metadata-driven access to an enterprise data lake. Exposing a new dataset requires only a JSON file, with no per-dataset integration code.

entry.title: Govern AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 2
entry.summary: In Part 1 you built one governed agent. Part 2 scales the pattern to an enterprise: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes the single front door and redeems Okta's grant, Cedar policies bind each tool to the agent, a second agent runs on Amazon EKS, and AgentCore Observability traces every allow and deny beside Okta's log in Amazon CloudWatch.

entry.title: Govern AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 1
entry.summary: An AI agent that acts for a user raises an identity question that per-app OAuth and service accounts leave open: which agent may act for which user, and how you stop it. In this first post of two, you build a task agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that governs access through Okta Cross App Access and AgentCore Identity, and enforces each user's authority.

entry.title: How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Greenlight Financial resolves more than 90% of up to 4,000 monthly security and risk cases without human intervention using Luna, a tiered multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post covers the architecture, episodic memory for continuous learning, and the expansion from SOC operations into financial risk triage.

entry.title: Taxbit Assist: A grounded, role-aware AI agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Taxbit built Taxbit Assist, a cited, permission-aware AI assistant embedded in its enterprise dashboard, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post shows how they grounded answers in a curated knowledge base, enforced role-aware and region-compliant safety, and continuously measured answer quality on live production traffic.

entry.title: Extend Claude Code to remote sessions on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with security controls
entry.summary: Run Claude Code as a remote agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each coding task runs in its own isolated session in your AWS account, every model call goes through Amazon Bedrock, and the result comes back as a GitHub pull request you review and merge.

entry.title: Getting started with Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore returns a synthesized, source-cited answer to a natural-language question in a single tool call, with no search, retrieve, synthesize, and citation pipeline to build. Learn how it works and how to add it to an AgentCore Gateway and call it from an agent.

entry.title: How Amazon Marketplace evaluates content quality with Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: Learn how Amazon Marketplace evaluates A+ Content quality at scale on Amazon SageMaker AI by rendering each product page as a single snapshot, scoring it with a vision-language model fused with OCR readability signals in a CatBoost classifier, and using SHAP to turn each decision into prioritized, actionable recommendations for selling partners.

entry.title: Use decision models with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
entry.summary: Some agent-evaluation questions are narrow and repeatable, and decision models answer exactly that kind of question. This post shows how to connect two decision models, Jev and Strands Decider, to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations through code-based evaluators, and how to validate a decision-model check before you gate a release on it.

entry.title: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick: Human oversight where it matters
entry.summary: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick reviews eligible agent actions within your existing controls, reducing unnecessary approval prompts while keeping consequential decisions with a person. See how policy sets the boundary, how a classifier reviews actions, and how AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Logs support audit.

entry.title: Four layers of context engineering for production AI agents: How Deep Insight applies them in working code
entry.summary: In production AI agents, context management is the real bottleneck. This post presents a four-layer context engineering framework (architecture, prompts, file-based tools, and verification agents), implemented in working code from Deep Insight, an open source multi-agent data analysis solution on the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

entry.title: How Indegene is modernizing and scaling enterprise data quality in life sciences
entry.summary: This post explores how Indegene built a production-grade, LLM-powered Data Quality Agent in its NEXT Unified Data Platform on AWS. The agent generates context-aware data quality rules, validates them, and produces ready-to-run SQL and Python under human-in-the-loop governance, helping life sciences organizations scale enterprise data quality.

entry.title: How U Mobile built agentic telco operations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: U Mobile, Malaysia's newest 5G network provider, built AiDaH, an agentic AI operations platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that moves beyond AI assistance to autonomous action across telco operations. Nine months after production launch, AiDaH handles over 150 operational scenarios across six divisions, cutting trouble tickets by up to 84.5%.

entry.title: Bring structured and unstructured data together with Amazon Quick
entry.summary: Amazon Quick brings structured and unstructured data together in one experience. In this post, you connect Amazon S3 as a knowledge base, enrich a dataset, build a Space, and create a custom chat agent that answers business questions across both data types through a single conversational interface.

entry.title: ServiceNow on-behalf-of token exchange with Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
entry.summary: Learn how to configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway for an on-behalf-of (OBO) token exchange with Microsoft Entra ID, so an AI agent can call the ServiceNow REST API while preserving the calling user's identity. AgentCore Gateway performs the exchange natively, with no interceptor Lambda or custom code.

entry.title: How Gen Digital built Norton Revamp’s AI-curated News Engine with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search
entry.summary: Gen Digital built Norton Revamp, a generative AI-powered professional reputation management platform, with an AI-curated News Engine grounded by Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See how the Gen team delivers real-time, cited content suggestions, goal setting, and news feeds with zero data egress and Norton-grade privacy.

entry.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI with EDB Postgres AI and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Learn how to build a governed semantic layer for agentic AI inside EDB Postgres AI and query it from a Strands Agents agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Business meaning, join paths, and access control all live in Postgres, with GRANT and row-level security enforcing what each agent can read.

entry.title: Building ultra-low-latency voice AI applications on AWS
entry.summary: Learn how Cartesia, an AWS Partner, uses purpose-built State Space Models and AWS infrastructure to deliver sub-100ms text-to-speech and speech-to-text at global scale, and how to deploy its Sonic model on Amazon SageMaker AI or self-managed Amazon EC2 GPU instances.

entry.title: Introducing India-based inference for Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock now offers in-country inference in India for Kimi K3, keeping processing within the Mumbai and Hyderabad Regions. This post explains the global and geographic cross-Region inference options and shares example code for reading and understanding Indic-language documents with Kimi K3.

entry.title: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI
entry.summary: This post shows how to use Crawl4AI, an open source web crawler, as a content preparation layer for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, handling JavaScript rendering, selective extraction, and custom metadata enrichment before web content reaches an Amazon S3 data source.

entry.title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: Agentic assistants built on frontier models run a multi-step tool loop, and paying frontier prices on every step is hard to sustain at production scale. This post shows how to use sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD) to transfer a frontier teacher's agentic behavior into a small, lower-cost student on Amazon SageMaker AI.

entry.title: Agentic engineering intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Learn how to build a multi-agent engineering assistant that compresses aerospace component substitution evaluation from days to minutes, using Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Strands Agents SDK to assemble substitution evidence while keeping the engineer as the decision-maker.

entry.title: How Circle K accelerated DevOps incident triage to under 15 minutes with Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Circle K's DevOps team cut incident triage from 45-60 minutes to under 15 by building an agentic triage system on Amazon Bedrock. This post walks through the architecture, the initial Amazon Bedrock Flows implementation, the migration to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the lessons learned from scaling it.

entry.title: Managing Amazon Bedrock costs end to end: A playbook for FinOps and platform teams
entry.summary: This post presents a five-stage operating model for managing Amazon Bedrock cost: attribute every dollar to an owner, make every request observable, enforce budgets, optimize platform defaults, and operate a review cadence. Written for FinOps and platform engineering teams.

entry.title: Preview web apps live as your coding agent builds them with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Session endpoints give each runtime session an authenticated URL that forwards any HTTP method, path, and WebSocket connection to the ports you allow. In this post, you deploy a coding agent that keeps a Vite website running in its session, then watch the live site update in your browser as the agent edits files.

entry.title: How Worldwide Express automated freight exceptions with Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Worldwide Express automated its less-than-truckload freight billing-exception process with a multi-agent solution built on Amazon Bedrock. Six months after launch, the company cut active exceptions by 75%, improved time-to-cash by four weeks, and unlocked $10 million in free cash flow.

entry.title: Configure the ChatGPT desktop app with Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)
entry.summary: The ChatGPT desktop app is now available on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US). This post walks through a controlled local deployment that routes model inference to Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-West) using API-mode sign-in, a managed device policy, a named AWS profile, and network restrictions, so a security team can validate it before broader use.

entry.title: How the UK Amazon Quick User Group grew in 2026
entry.summary: The UK Amazon Quick User Group's 2026 roundup: three quarterly meetups, 150+ attendees, and customer stories from Arriva, Carsa, and Propulse Lab on using agentic AI and Amazon Quick to turn data into faster decisions, higher satisfaction, and scalable growth.

entry.title: Building intent-driven UI testing with Amazon Nova Act
entry.summary: Epsilon's Agentic Platform team delivers UI testing as a managed, multi-tenant service built on Amazon Nova Act and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool. Tests are written in plain English and run on browsers managed by AWS, giving every product team resilient, intent-driven testing with zero per-team infrastructure overhead.

entry.title: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro
entry.summary: Turn a PHP-to-Java migration from a one-time leap of faith into a measurable, repeatable process with Kiro. This post walks through a reusable engine: a mechanical discovery scanner and an eight-phase, parity-first workflow that treats the original PHP application as the specification and verifies the Java port with a parity harness.

entry.title: Lend and borrow resources across teams with AWS Batch’s quota management for SageMaker Training jobs
entry.summary: AWS Batch quota management is a new scheduling capability you can use to divide GPU capacity into quota shares per team or project, automatically lend idle capacity across shares, and use preemption to run your highest-priority SageMaker Training jobs first, all without manual coordination.

entry.title: How MoEngage turned over 400 APIs into agent tools with AgentCore Gateway
entry.summary: MoEngage turned roughly 400 private REST APIs across 7 AWS Regions into permission-scoped agent tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. No per-service MCP servers, no public endpoints, and no 400-tool context bloat. See how OpenAPI specs, Cedar policies, and managed Amazon VPC Lattice egress made it work.

entry.title: Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS
entry.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model that pairs reasoning and tool use with multimodal understanding. This post explores its architecture and use cases, then shows how to deploy it on Amazon EKS, EKS Auto Mode, and Amazon SageMaker HyperPod EKS with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM.

entry.title: Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Stand up a governed, multi-account Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post walks through the architecture and an open-source reference blueprint: the operating model, control plane, per-Workstream cells, separate inference and tool gateways, and a CI/CD evaluation pipeline that gates each agent before production.

entry.title: Distributed training with Ray Train DLCs and EFA on EKS
entry.summary: The Ray Train Deep Learning Container ships the full CUDA-through-EFA stack, so you build no image. This post walks through a reproducible sample that fine-tunes Qwen2.5-1.5B with PyTorch FSDP across eight GPUs on two EFA-enabled g6.12xlarge instances on Amazon EKS, using the container exactly as published.

entry.title: Accelerating software delivery with agentic QA automation using Amazon Nova Act – Part 3
entry.summary: As QA test automation spreads across an organization, organizing tests and controlling who owns them becomes the real work. Part 3 of the QA Studio series on Amazon Nova Act adds applications that organize tests and report health metrics, plus team-based user management that controls who can see and change what.

entry.title: AWS named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service
entry.summary: AWS has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) for AWS Connect Customer. This recognition marks an important milestone for our team, and it reflects years of work pushing on what's possible in customer experience.

entry.title: Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs
entry.summary: Seekable OCI (SOCI) indexing for Amazon SageMaker AI training and processing jobs takes full container image download off the critical path. SageMaker AI lazy-loads your image to start containers in seconds instead of minutes, with no changes to your job definition. See the benchmarks and how to adopt it.

entry.title: Fix evaluation bias to unlock better models on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Property Finder found that 96.8% of their vision-AI evaluation labels were inherited from the incumbent model, hiding its true accuracy. See how they built unbiased ground truth, applied evolutionary prompt optimization, and selected a more accurate, cost-effective model on Amazon Bedrock, cutting cost by 86% across 11 image-quality attributes.

entry.title: Exowatt beats frontier models on accuracy with SageMaker serverless model customization
entry.summary: In this post, we show how Exowatt used Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization to build a repeatable AI pipeline that produces task-specific fine-tuned models for two deployment targets, edge and cloud, achieving higher accuracy than frontier models at up to 49x lower cost.

entry.title: Fleet-wide computer vision lifecycle at the edge with SageMaker SDK v3
entry.summary: Fleet-wide computer vision needs a model per camera, not one model for the whole fleet. This post presents a working Amazon SageMaker SDK v3 reference architecture that trains, quality-gates, compiles per-camera models with SageMaker Neo, and versions thousands of them, with an AWS Step Functions layer pacing fleet-scale retraining within account quotas.

entry.title: Groundhog Day for AI agents: Prompt caching patterns for using OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Every time an agent takes a step, it re-reads its entire context before acting. Here is how prompt caching for OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock lets your agent remember, cutting input cost and latency without resending the same tools, instructions, and history every turn.

entry.title: Build agentic retrieval on a Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with CDK
entry.summary: Build enterprise agentic retrieval on a Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with the AWS CDK: an agent that routes across two knowledge bases, retrieves through the AgentCore Gateway, and returns grounded, cited answers, with seven layers of observability and both on-demand and continuous evaluation, all deployed as a single CDK application.

entry.title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide
entry.summary: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI trains models on the outcome of a whole multi-step task rather than labeled steps. This hands-on guide walks the full pipeline using Wordle: deploying the agent and reward on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, preparing the dataset, training, and evaluating at serving settings.

entry.title: Orchestrating SageMaker AI endpoint auto scaling with AWS CDK
entry.summary: Updating a SageMaker AI endpoint that has Application Auto Scaling registered makes AWS CloudFormation and AWS CDK deployments fail. This post shows how to build a reusable AWS CDK construct with CloudFormation custom resources that deregisters and re-registers auto scaling automatically, so you can update the endpoint and its scaling in a single deployment.

entry.title: Visualize points and routes with GeoJSON in Amazon Quick Sight layer maps
entry.summary: Amazon Quick Sight layer maps now support Point and LineString geometry from the same GeoJSON workflow, so you can plot store locations and the routes between them. This post covers the dataset and GeoJSON structure layer maps require, when to choose points or lines, and techniques for viewport control, layering geometries, and dynamic GeoJSON updates.

entry.title: How Bayer Crop Science built an agentic decision engine on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with AWS Unified Operations
entry.summary: Bayer Crop Science built the Agentic Decision Engine (ADE), a multi-agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that lets breeders, analysts, and researchers ask natural language questions about their analytics platform. This post covers the ADE architecture, five design decisions, and how the team prepared it for production with AWS Unified Operations.

entry.title: Amazon Polly delivers a major upgrade to its Generative engine
entry.summary: The Amazon Polly Generative engine gets a major upgrade: more expressive, more accurate speech with low latency, plus 14 new voices across 9 locales and general availability of Hindi and Finnish. This drop-in upgrade requires no code changes and is now generally available in production.

entry.title: How IskayPet unified corporate knowledge with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases
entry.summary: Learn how IskayPet, a leading pet care company in Iberia, built a multilingual corporate knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases. The assistant answers employee questions across retail, veterinary, onboarding, and procurement in four languages and three countries, with no RAG infrastructure to manage.

entry.title: Announcing new ways to customize models with SageMaker AI, without managing GPUs
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization now includes training sessions, generally available today. You write and coordinate your own post-training loop (custom loss functions, reward signals, or multi-turn reinforcement learning) while SageMaker AI handles GPU allocation, distributed execution, fault recovery, and checkpoint storage.

entry.title: Write your own training loop — without managing GPUs — with Amazon SageMaker training session APIs
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI training session APIs let you write your own LLM training loop (SFT, RL, or custom objectives) in a Python script while the service runs the GPUs. This post introduces the programming model and three SDK clients, then walks through a GRPO loop on GSM8K and a reinforcement learning workload on competitive programming.

entry.title: Deploy AI in a HIPAA-eligible environment with Amazon Quick
entry.summary: Amazon Quick is a HIPAA-eligible service, but eligibility is not the same as compliance. This post explains who HIPAA applies to, how PHI flows through Amazon Quick, what the platform provides for regulated environments, and a step-by-step guide to deploying compliant AI agents in a healthcare environment.

entry.title: Stream low-latency speech from AI agents using Kokoro TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: Voice agents often wait for an agent's full response before starting speech synthesis, adding latency users feel directly. This post shows how to stream each sentence to a Kokoro-82M text-to-speech model on Amazon SageMaker AI as the agent produces it, and how to get that audio back to a browser over Server-Sent Events or a unified binary transport.

entry.title: Stop guessing auto scaling targets for TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: Teams deploying custom text-to-speech models on Amazon SageMaker AI often guess at autoscaling thresholds, and a wrong guess either wastes GPU spend or breaches a latency SLO. This post deploys Kokoro-82M as a custom container and derives a measured autoscaling policy from two live-endpoint measurements, Q_max and T_total, instead of guesswork.

entry.title: How Rescale built an AI triage agent with Strands Agents and AI-DLC
entry.summary: Rescale used the AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) framework on AWS, with Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock, to build an intelligent test-triage agent in weeks. Learn how AI-DLC structures AI-assisted development and how Rescale is scaling the practice across its engineering organization.

entry.title: Securing Quick access from corporate networks with AWS PrivateLink
entry.summary: Learn how to connect on-premises data sources to Amazon Quick privately with AWS PrivateLink, keeping analytics traffic off the public internet. This walkthrough covers VPC endpoints for user and API access, VPC connections for data sources, DNS and endpoint policies, identity federation, and enforcing VPC-endpoint-only access for compliance.

entry.title: 5 production challenges in multi-agent systems and how Deep Insight solved them
entry.summary: Many teams build a multi-agent AI prototype in days but hit a wall in production. This post defines five production challenges (orchestration, per-agent model selection, reliable operation, secure code execution, and monitoring) and shows how Deep Insight, an open source multi-agent system on AWS, solves each.

entry.title: Adaptive agentic intelligence framework using Strands Agents
entry.summary: The Adaptive Agentic Intelligence Framework (AAIF), built with Strands Agents, handles routine tasks locally with small language models and routes complex requests to cloud models through Amazon Bedrock. This post walks through building AAIF with local SLMs through Ollama and Amazon Bedrock, using an Internet of Things monitoring scenario.

entry.title: Train Qwen3 on AWS Trainium with torchtitan
entry.summary: Train Qwen3 on AWS Trainium with torchtitan three ways on a single trn2.48xlarge: the Hugging Face Transformers v5 modeling backend, torchtitan's native Qwen3, and NKI mixture-of-experts kernels. The same torchrun launcher and config structure work unchanged across all three paths, including loading and saving published Hugging Face safetensors.

entry.title: How U.S. Hunger connects leaders and data using Amazon Quick
entry.summary: U.S. Hunger, a nonprofit addressing food insecurity, uses Amazon Quick to connect organizational data with leadership decisions. Leaders explore applicant data directly, share KPI definitions and financial context in Quick Spaces, and investigate policy questions with Quick Research.

entry.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
entry.summary: Learn how i14 trained and served Laplace 3B, a linear attention model, on AWS Trainium2 using native PyTorch. Its recurrent state stays fixed at 29.5 MB per sequence regardless of context length, avoiding the growing key-value cache of transformer models and keeping serving memory predictable.

entry.title: Workflow context for AI agents with Smartsheet MCP on AWS
entry.summary: The Smartsheet Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server lets AI agents read, update, and act on live data. This post shows two ways to connect it on AWS: Amazon Quick for business teams and Kiro for developers, so your agents can work with Smartsheet without switching tools.

entry.title: Work management context for AI agents with Smartsheet MCP on AWS
entry.summary: The Smartsheet Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server lets AI agents read, update, and act on live work management data. This post shows two ways to connect it on AWS: Amazon Quick for business teams and Kiro for developers, so your agents can work with Smartsheet without switching tools.

entry.title: From data to decisions: Conversational supply chain intelligence with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Enterprise supply chains are data-rich but insight-poor, with the data to decide scattered across ERP, monitoring, procurement, and email. This post shows how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore exposes those systems as a governed tool layer, and how Amazon Quick turns them into one conversational experience for business users, with a deploy-it-yourself walkthrough.

entry.title: Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
entry.summary: Learn how we fine-tuned GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, and how to decide between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with GRPO. SFT took reasoning-language accuracy from 22% to 100%, and GRPO added measurable gains where headroom existed.

entry.title: How Octave built a secure multi-tenant AI foundation on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Octave built a secure, multi-tenant AI foundation on Amazon Bedrock, using Cohere Embed v4 for embeddings and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for isolated agent execution, to power a Complaint Triage Assistant that searches 2 billion regulated documents without crossing tenant boundaries.

entry.title: Access OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock from Canada with cross-Region inference
entry.summary: Canadian organizations can now access OpenAI GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 models on Amazon Bedrock from the Canada (Central) and Canada West (Calgary) Regions using cross-Region inference. This post covers the models and inference profiles, how to set up permissions, and how to invoke them with the Responses, Chat Completions, and Converse APIs.

entry.title: Discover tools at runtime with AWS Agent Registry
entry.summary: Hardcoded tool wiring breaks down as an agent's catalog grows from a handful of tools to hundreds. This post walks through a runtime Discover, Instantiate, Execute loop built on AWS Agent Registry, where an orchestrator discovers MCP servers and A2A agents through semantic search at runtime instead of compiling every tool at build time.

entry.title: Securing AI agent identity with X.509 PKI on AWS
entry.summary: Learn how to secure multi-agent AI systems with cryptographic identity using Keyfactor EJBCA and AWS services. This reference architecture combines signed request envelopes, user-signed delegation assertions, RFC 8693 audience-scoped tokens, and real-time OCSP revocation to prove agent identity and prevent request forgery across agent-to-agent and MCP tool calls.

entry.title: How Eon built multi-cloud investigation with an MCP Gateway on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Learn how Eon replaced per-tool credentials and local MCP processes across AWS, GCP, and Azure with a single authenticated Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, giving more than 100 developers and autonomous agents unified access to production investigation and cutting new-engineer onboarding from two days to two minutes.

entry.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with Denodo and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Build a governed semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with the Denodo Platform and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. It federates Amazon Aurora, Amazon Redshift, and an on-premises PostgreSQL database into a single customer 360 view an agent queries in VQL, with identity propagation and row- and column-level access control enforced at the semantic layer.

entry.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with Strategy Mosaic and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: The third post in our semantic-layer series builds a customer 360 across Amazon Redshift and Amazon Aurora with Strategy Mosaic, exposes it to a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore through the Mosaic MCP server, and enforces per-user row and column security end-to-end.

entry.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with AtScale and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: The third post in our semantic-layer series builds a governed customer 360 model on Amazon Redshift with AtScale, then exposes it to a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore through the AtScale MCP server. Identity propagation, RBAC, row security, and full query audit are enforced at the semantic layer, not the prompt.

entry.title: Structured outputs for Anthropic Claude models on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models on both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints. Receive schema-compliant JSON that conforms to a defined structure, without custom parsing, retry logic, or post-processing, using JSON Schema output format and strict tool use.

entry.title: Developers can now access SageMaker Studio through the new AWS experience
entry.summary: New Amazon SageMaker AI customers can now land in a fully configured SageMaker Studio environment in only a few steps. Sign up with an identity you already have, such as Amazon, Apple, GitHub, or Google, with no advanced AWS account or credit card required for most customers, plus $100 in AWS Free Tier credits.

entry.title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: 2026 year-to-date in review
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart onboarded over 100 new models from 30 providers in the first three quarters of 2026. This recap covers the model-onboarding highlights and JumpStart enhancements, including the simplified Model Hub, pre-configured deployment options, and Hugging Face deep link integration.

entry.title: Pegasus 1.5 from TwelveLabs is now available in Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: TwelveLabs Pegasus 1.5 is now available in Amazon Bedrock. The video language model turns long-form video into structured, timestamped metadata: define the moments that matter and get every matching segment back as JSON, with new video segmentation, multimodal prompting with reference images, and on-the-fly processing of up to two hours of video.

entry.title: How Deepgram optimized voice AI at scale with AWS Trainium
entry.summary: Deepgram worked with the AWS Forward Deployed Engineering team to port its Nova-3 speech-to-text model to AWS Trainium2 for offline batch inference. This post covers porting to the AWS Neuron stack, kernel-level tuning, a data-parallel Rust runtime, and the throughput and cost results on batch transcription.

entry.title: Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM
entry.summary: vLLM's prefill-decode disaggregation splits LLM inference across engine instances but must transfer the KV cache between them. This post introduces a push-based NIXL connector that moves transfer coordination off the critical path, delivering up to 3x better TTFT and 30% better TPOT in benchmarks on Amazon EC2 P5en instances with AWS EFA.

entry.title: Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM
entry.summary: Multi-turn agentic workloads reprocess growing conversation context each turn, driving up latency. See how bi-directional KV cache transfer lets prefill and decode nodes reuse previously computed context across turns, cutting time to first token by up to 1.6x for Qwen3-32B and 3.3x for GLM-5-FP8 on Amazon EC2 P5en instances with EFA.

entry.title: SRE Weekly Issue #539
entry.summary: View on sreweekly.com A message from our sponsor, Incident.io: AI made shipping code faster. Now reliability is the bottleneck. Hear how Netflix and OpenAI handle that challenge at SEV0, the reliability conference in SF and London. Free for SREWeekly readers with code SREWEEKLY. Claim your free pass → Hot take Today, I learned that “hot […]

entry.title: Building trust in AI agents: A production-ready evaluation framework with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Autonomous AI agents fail softly: latency stays flat while answer quality quietly erodes. This post shares a nine-stage evaluation framework, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, that catches silent quality regressions across the full agent lifecycle, from first commit to live production.

entry.title: Introducing Reflection Beam: an open-weight model for agentic coding on AWS
entry.summary: Reflection AI's Beam is an open-weight model for agentic coding and long-horizon tasks. This post shows how to deploy Beam on AWS: start with an Amazon SageMaker JumpStart real-time endpoint, or use Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference with JumpStart, SGLang, or vLLM for Kubernetes-native control over distributed GPU infrastructure.

entry.title: Meta’s Muse Spark Open now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
entry.summary: Muse Spark Open, Meta's coding-optimized open-weight model, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. Deploy it to a SageMaker AI endpoint in your own AWS account using SageMaker Studio or the SageMaker Python SDK, and run your first inference request.

entry.title: Trust in Depth: Giving agents more autonomy without losing control
entry.summary: Enterprise leaders want AI agents to take on more work but don't fully trust them to act correctly every time. Trust in Depth is AWS's layered approach-scope, know, bound, observe, and prove-that lets agents act on their own when their actions can be verified, reserving human judgment for the decisions that need it.

entry.title: Build self-improving document processing using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Learn how to build an agentic intelligent document processing (IDP) system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that classifies, extracts, validates, and learns from business documents with minimal human intervention, automatically handling new document formats without manual template configuration.

entry.title: Generate presentations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: This post walks you through building an AI agent system with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that automates PowerPoint presentation creation from enterprise documents. A supervisor agent, Retrieval Augmented Generation, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails generate grounded presentations in under 90 seconds.

entry.title: How Tamnoon built AI-powered cloud security remediation with Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Learn how Tamnoon built Tami, an agentic cloud remediation orchestrator on Amazon Bedrock that autonomously investigates and safely remediates cloud security findings from CNAPP and cloud-native sources. The approach drove a 90%+ reduction in critical cloud exposure in 90 days with zero production issues.

entry.title: Deploy and evaluate models with Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
entry.summary: Learn how to deploy an available model from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, run a lightweight and repeatable performance test using the SageMaker Python SDK, and delete the endpoint when testing is complete.

entry.title: Building agents that transact with Anchor Browser and AgentCore payments
entry.summary: Learn how the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center Partner Agent Factory and Anchor Browser built AI agents that autonomously pay for x402-protected web resources and APIs. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments checks budgets, signs transactions, and retries requests without exposing wallet credentials to the agent runtime.

entry.title: Manage private pricing offers for Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements
entry.summary: Managing AI model access across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts creates friction when each account must accept AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offers individually. This post shows two ways to activate MPPO entitlements in AWS License Manager: a lightweight script for a one-time fix, and CDK automation for ongoing event-driven processing.

entry.title: Natural language security queries at Orca Security using Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Orca Security built Discovery AI, a natural language query agent on Amazon Bedrock that converts plain-English questions into Sonar queries. The post shares the multi-stage architecture and the results: 90% lower query cost, 93% fewer input tokens, and 75% lower latency than the initial baseline.

entry.title: How ShipStation Global built an AI IT help desk on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: ShipStation Global's engineering team built Deckhand, an AI IT help desk agent for Slack on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. It answers routine IT questions from a curated knowledge base, reads error-message screenshots, and files Jira tickets. In its first three months it resolved 97.5% of channel queries with a 96% positive feedback rating.

entry.title: Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock. In this post, we build a tool-calling agent on Grok 4.7 and evaluate it on three reasoning tasks at four reasoning effort levels, measuring correctness and token cost per completed task. We show how to tune the trade-off per request and monitor it in production.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: AWS engineers share kernel optimizations for fused Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models on Amazon SageMaker AI: Swap-AB for WGMMA utilization, Triton backend routing for FP8 quantization, and eliminating Triton JIT recompilation. Together they deliver up to 10% higher throughput and up to 9% faster Time to First Token on H200 GPUs.
